questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^2}\,dx\), or state that it diverges.
questions.answer: We need to replace the infinite endpoint with a limit. Write \(\int_1^\infty x^{-2}\,dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\int_1^b x^{-2}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(-x^{-1}\). Thus the integral equals \(\lim_{b\to\infty}[-\frac{1}{x}]_1^b=\lim_{b\to\infty}(-\frac{1}{b}+1)=1\). Therefore the improper integral converges to \(1\).

We need to test the infinite endpoint with a limit. Write \(\int_1^\infty\frac{1}{x}\,dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\int_1^b\frac{1}{x}\,dx\). The antiderivative is \(\ln x\). Thus the expression is \(\lim_{b\to\infty}(\ln b-\ln1)=\lim_{b\to\infty}\ln b\). Since \(\ln b\to\infty\), the integral diverges.

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int_0^1 \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), or state that it diverges.
questions.answer: We need to handle the infinite value at \(x=0\). Write \(\int_0^1 x^{-1/2}\,dx=\lim_{a\to0^+}\int_a^1 x^{-1/2}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(2x^{1/2}\). The value is \(\lim_{a\to0^+}[2\sqrt{x}]_a^1=\lim_{a\to0^+}(2-2\sqrt{a})=2\). Therefore the improper integral converges to \(2\).

We need to test the singularity at \(x=0\). Write \(\int_0^1 x^{-2}\,dx=\lim_{a\to0^+}\int_a^1 x^{-2}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(-x^{-1}\). Evaluate: \(\lim_{a\to0^+}[-\frac{1}{x}]_a^1=\lim_{a\to0^+}(-1+\frac{1}{a})\). Since \(\frac{1}{a}\to\infty\), the integral diverges.

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,dx\), or state that it diverges.
questions.answer: We need to use a limit for the infinite interval. Write \(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\int_0^b e^{-x}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(-e^{-x}\). Therefore the value is \(\lim_{b\to\infty}[-e^{-x}]_0^b=\lim_{b\to\infty}(-e^{-b}+1)\). Since \(e^{-b}\to0\), the integral converges to \(1\).

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(\int_2^\infty \frac{1}{x^3}\,dx\) converges, and find its value if it converges.
questions.answer: We need to evaluate an infinite-interval integral. Write \(\int_2^\infty x^{-3}\,dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\int_2^b x^{-3}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(-\frac{1}{2x^2}\). Evaluate: \(\lim_{b\to\infty}[-\frac{1}{2x^2}]_2^b=\lim_{b\to\infty}(-\frac{1}{2b^2}+\frac{1}{8})=\frac{1}{8}\). Therefore the integral converges to \(\frac{1}{8}\).

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int_{-\infty}^{0} e^x\,dx\), or state that it diverges.
questions.answer: We need to replace the lower infinite endpoint with a limit. Write \(\int_{-\infty}^{0}e^x\,dx=\lim_{a\to-\infty}\int_a^0 e^x\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(e^x\). Thus the value is \(\lim_{a\to-\infty}[e^x]_a^0=\lim_{a\to-\infty}(1-e^a)\). Since \(e^a\to0\) as \(a\to-\infty\), the integral converges to \(1\).

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx\) converges, and find its value if it converges.
questions.answer: We need to split the integral at a finite point because both endpoints are infinite. Use \(0\): \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx=\int_{-\infty}^0\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx+\int_0^{\infty}\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(\arctan x\). The first part is \(\lim_{a\to-\infty}(\arctan0-\arctan a)=0-(-\frac{\pi}{2})=\frac{\pi}{2}\). The second part is \(\lim_{b\to\infty}(\arctan b-\arctan0)=\frac{\pi}{2}\). The total is \(\pi\), so the integral converges to \(\pi\).

questions.prompt: For which values of \(p\) does \(\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^p}\,dx\) converge?
questions.answer: We need the convergence condition for a \(p\)-integral. For \(p\ne1\), \(\int_1^b x^{-p}\,dx=\frac{b^{1-p}-1}{1-p}\). If \(p>1\), then \(1-p<0\), so \(b^{1-p}\to0\), giving a finite limit. If \(p<1\), then \(b^{1-p}\to\infty\), so the integral diverges. For \(p=1\), the integral is \(\int_1^\infty\frac{1}{x}\,dx\), which diverges like \(\ln b\). Therefore the integral converges exactly when \(p>1\).

questions.prompt: Evaluate \(\int_0^4 \frac{1}{\sqrt{4-x}}\,dx\), or state that it diverges.
questions.answer: We need to handle the singularity at \(x=4\). Write \(\int_0^4(4-x)^{-1/2}\,dx=\lim_{b\to4^-}\int_0^b(4-x)^{-1/2}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(-2\sqrt{4-x}\), because differentiating gives \((4-x)^{-1/2}\). Evaluate: \(\lim_{b\to4^-}[-2\sqrt{4-x}]_0^b=\lim_{b\to4^-}(-2\sqrt{4-b}+4)\). As \(b\to4^-\), \(\sqrt{4-b}\to0\), so the value is \(4\). Therefore the improper integral converges to \(4\).
